one_sentence_story: A source card crosses a custody corridor: each beat makes one visible transformation, but the final S6 paper claim closes only when its ordinal trail can be replayed and falsified.

beats.title: Source enters
beats.visual: A warm paper source card stands on the left basalt island. One clearly legible source-pointer line lights up, then emits a single amber filament toward the center.
beats.source_pointer: W1-MANIFEST.json source_set; this beat asserts no world event

beats.title: Context separates
beats.visual: The amber filament enters a transparent Context Capsule. Inside it, an amber source rail remains distinct from a cyan claim token; they never merge into one undifferentiated glow.
beats.on_screen_copy: CONTEXT IS A BOUNDARY, NOT PROOF
beats.source_pointer: G-VITRIN/3B1B-ANLATI-BILGI.md Rule 7: flag approximations and say what the animation does not prove

beats.title: Object persists
beats.visual: Three concentric torus rings form around the same cyan claim token. The token keeps its orientation and label while the camera does not cut; the amber source rail stays visible behind the capsule.
beats.causal_move: claim token -> persistent object with provenance

beats.title: World trace replays
beats.visual: The cyan token exits the capsule along a blue filament that touches three fixed hexagonal fibre cusps in order. Each cusp leaves a small receipt tab; the terrain reads as a traversable world, not a dashboard.
beats.on_screen_copy: A CLAIM NEEDS A REPLAYABLE TRACE
beats.source_pointer: P-HERAKLES-PAPER/DRAFT-FINAL.md Section 07 lines 624-628: memory is described as traversable world; receipt and world event remain required future witnesses

beats.title: Claim closes with a brake
beats.visual: At the right scroll, the torus aperture closes into a hexagonal seal beside a readable receipt card. The wording visibly labels the statement as a paper claim and places its refuter on the same card.
beats.causal_move: ordered trace + receipt -> qualified paper claim
beats.on_screen_copy: PAPER CLAIM / S6: EON = ORDINAL EVENT ORDER / NOT WALL CLOCK
beats.secondary_copy: REFUTE IF ORDER DEPENDS ONLY ON WALL TIME
beats.source_pointer: P-HERAKLES-PAPER/DRAFT-FINAL.md Section 06 lines 484-506; claim is not presented as consensus fact

persistent_objects.continuity: fixed left anchor from beat 1 through beat 5
persistent_objects.receipt_requirement: show a real source pointer in a later production pass; this concept does not invent one

persistent_objects.continuity: one unbroken path from source-card into capsule; source rail never recolors into the claim token
center anchor; contains the claim token and preserves source/claim separation
three rings are created once in beat 3 and remain attached to the same token
three fixed cusps receive the exiting filament in event order
tabs accumulate at trace cusps; they are not evidence until backed by a real receipt

caption_script: A context capsule separates what was observed from what is claimed.
The claim token stays the same object while its provenance stays attached.
A world trace gives the claim an ordered path that can be replayed.
The paper's S6 claim is qualified: EON is proposed as ordinal event order, not a wall clock; the trace must remain falsifiable.

render.camera: fixed orthographic ThreeDCamera at (0, 0, 15), focal point (0, 0, 0), no cuts

geometry: source-card = Polygon with fixed points [(-6.35,-1.35,0),(-5.15,-1.05,0),(-5.05,0.65,0),(-6.25,0.45,0)] plus Text source pointer
amber-stream = ParametricFunction over fixed cubic Bezier control points [(-5.05,-0.55,0),(-3.0,-1.25,0),(-1.55,0.85,0),(-0.35,0.0,0)]
context-capsule = transparent RoundedRectangle width 2.25 height 2.8 corner_radius 0.12 stroke cyan opacity 0.7
claim-token = cyan RegularPolygon(n=6, radius=0.42) with a smaller diamond cutout; label uses Text, never generated texture
torus-family = three deterministic Torus objects with major_radius [0.85, 1.08, 1.31], minor_radius 0.075, fixed rotations [0, PI/6, -PI/6]
cusp-fibre = three RegularPolygon(n=6, radius 0.30) objects with one fixed V-shaped inward cusp line; no noise or random displacement
blue-trace = ParametricFunction over fixed cubic Bezier control points [(-0.15,0.0,0), (1.2,0.55,0), (3.35,-1.0,0), (5.65,-0.4,0)]
receipt-card = white Text group with exact copy from beat 5 and a fixed 3-row ruled tab

timeline.action: FadeIn source-card; Create amber-stream; reveal source pointer
MoveAlongPath amber-stream into capsule; FadeIn source rail and claim-token without changing source rail color
Create three torus rings; rotate each by a fixed angle over 30 frames; keep token and source-card stationary
Create blue-trace; MoveAlongPath token to cusp-fibre checkpoints; add one receipt-tab per checkpoint in order
Transform torus aperture into hex seal; FadeIn receipt-card and secondary falsifier copy; hold final state for 18 frames

determinism: set_seed(32) before scene construction even though no stochastic primitive is used
all paths, coordinates, colors, labels, durations, and rotations are constants
no image-text extraction, random particle field, dashboard widget, or unverified world payload
reduced_motion = render all final states at frame 0, preserve copy and object order, remove travel and rotation

falsifier.statement: This visual direction fails if the claimed EON order can only be reconstructed from wall-clock timestamps and cannot be replayed from an ordinal event sequence.
falsifier.test: Provide a real EON/world-event snapshot plus a render receipt; replay the trace with clock values hidden, then replay it with event order permuted.
falsifier.refuting_observation: If the same ordered result cannot be recovered without wall-clock values, or if permuting event order leaves the result unchanged, reject the S6 framing.
falsifier.evidence_boundary: The concept contains no world snapshot, event stream, or render receipt; ImageGen/reference pixels are not evidence.

local_receipts.observed: Section 06 states EON as ordinal/event-based and not wall-clock; lines 502-506 define the counter surface wording.
